fields.h1: Build a Forklift Operator Evaluation Form Scored on the Floor
fields.hero_description: Build a forklift operator evaluation form that scores each maneuver and saves a certification record for every operator.
fields.features_heading: What the Evaluator Scores and Saves
fields.features_subheading: The evaluator walks beside the operator with a tablet. Emergent builds the form they score and the record it leaves.
fields.feature_1:
Items written for each truck type

Emergent builds the evaluation from a plain-English list of the trucks you run. A reach truck gets its own items, like extending the pantograph, and you add more by asking.
fields.feature_2:
Pass or needs work on every maneuver

The evaluator marks each maneuver as it happens, such as the horn at a blind corner or parking with the forks down. A needs-work mark opens a box for what the evaluator saw.
fields.feature_3:
Two signatures close the evaluation

The app captures the evaluator's signature and the operator's on the tablet before the evaluation is saved. Each signature stays attached to the evaluation it was given for.
fields.feature_4:
The next due date, counted for you

The app stores each operator's evaluation date and shows the date three years on. Sort by that date to see who is next, or filter the list down to one site or one truck type.
fields.feature_5:
Every evaluation in a database you own

Each evaluation is saved as a row holding every score beside both of the names. Emergent sets no cap on responses, so years of records for a large crew stay in one place.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, exported on paid plans

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when evaluations need to sit next to your training records. Host it where you like and keep building.

fields.tab_content_1:
Pass all 12 maneuvers and the record is written

Tibor Mallinson walks each new hire at Gresford Freight through 12 maneuvers on a sit-down counterbalance truck, scoring each one on a tablet. Ebba Coakley passed all 12. Once both signed, the form wrote her certification record, with Tibor Mallinson as the evaluator.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three-year evaluations come due on a list

Orrin Bay Foods has 38 people cleared to drive across its cold storage sites. The board counts the days to each operator's three-year mark, and anyone within 60 days of it moves to the due list. This week Agnar Ruhle had 18 days left. Safety manager Gisele Dorsch got an email naming the 3 operators now on the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
After one near-miss, a refresher and a re-evaluation

Nobody was hurt when Zelig Grunwald's forks clipped a rack upright in aisle 7 at Strathy Paper. His shift lead logged the near-miss against his name that night. His status changed to refresher due, and training lead Fiadh Yeboah got a Slack direct message asking her to book his refresher training and a new evaluation.
fields.tab_content_4:
New truck type, new evaluation on that truck

Bartosz Quaid drove a sit-down counterbalance truck at Mordaunt Building Supply until he moved to the reach truck in the lumber shed. His record had no reach truck evaluation, so the form opened one with 10 items. Tegan Holmvik scored him on her phone, and he passed all 10. His record now lists both truck types.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Forklift Operator Evaluations
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a forklift operator evaluation form that scores operators on the floor and tracks when each is due again.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every truck type you run
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose two marks, not a points scale
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name the people who can evaluate
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every truck type your operators drive, such as a sit-down counterbalance truck, a reach truck, or an order picker. Give each one its own version of the evaluation, because a reach truck has a pantograph that a sit-down driver never touches.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the maneuvers an evaluator watches on each truck: the pre-use check, then every move a load makes between pickup and parking. Keep the list short enough that one evaluation fits into a single session in the operator's normal work area.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give the evaluator two marks for every maneuver, pass or needs work, instead of a points scale. Then decide what a needs-work mark leads to. One mark might mean a retest of that maneuver, while two or more might mean another round of practical training.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who is qualified to evaluate at your site, such as your lead trainer and the shift supervisors who train new drivers. Put those evaluators on the form as a list. Only a name from that list can sign an evaluation.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your truck types and scoring rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form with its certification record and its due-date board. Ask for a change later, like a new truck type, and Emergent makes it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run one evaluation as a test
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run one test evaluation with an experienced operator. Mark one maneuver as needs work on purpose and sign it. Check that the certification record and the due date look right before evaluators take the form onto the warehouse floor.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Set what brings an operator back
fields.howto_step_7_des: Set the events that put an operator back on the list, like a near-miss or a move to a new truck type. Add the three-year date from each operator's last evaluation as well, and choose who hears when a name lands on the list.

faq_plan.q: What is a forklift operator evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: A forklift operator evaluation form is the record an evaluator fills in while watching an operator drive a forklift at work. It lists the maneuvers for that truck type and marks each one pass or needs work. It ends with the evaluator's and the operator's signatures.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a forklift operator evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the truck types you run, the maneuvers to score, and who signs. Emergent builds the form along with the certification record and the board of due dates. Change any part later by asking, such as adding an order picker version.

faq_plan.q: How often should a forklift operator evaluation form be completed for each operator?
faq_plan.a: At least once every three years per operator. OSHA's rule says an evaluation of each operator's performance is conducted at least once every three years. Refresher training after an accident or near-miss also includes an evaluation of the effectiveness of that training, which adds a date to the operator's record.

faq_plan.q: Should a forklift operator evaluation form use pass or fail marks or a rating scale?
faq_plan.a: Pass or needs work suits a forklift evaluation, because the evaluator is judging whether each maneuver was done safely, not ranking operators. A rating scale fits a tryout evaluation form, where coaches compare players for a limited number of spots. Put a comment box on every needs-work mark to keep the reason on the record.

faq_plan.q: Who can fill out a forklift operator evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: Someone with the knowledge, training, and experience to train forklift operators and evaluate their competence. OSHA's rule says all operator training and evaluation are conducted by persons who have that background. Record the evaluator's name on every form, since it belongs on the operator's certification as well.

faq_plan.q: What should a forklift operator evaluation form record for certification?
faq_plan.a: The operator's name, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and who performed the training or evaluation. Those are the items OSHA's rule says the certification includes. In an app Emergent builds, each record is a row in a database you own, next to the scored evaluation it came from.

faq_plan.q: What happens after a needs-work mark on a forklift operator evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: It can send the operator to refresher training. OSHA's rule lists an evaluation that reveals the operator is not operating the truck safely as one reason refresher training is provided. Set the form to change the operator's status to refresher due on that mark, and the app alerts the training lead by email or in Slack.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a separate forklift operator evaluation form for each type of forklift?
faq_plan.a: Yes, one version per type keeps the scored maneuvers matched to the truck being driven. OSHA's rule lists being assigned to drive a different type of truck as a reason for refresher training, and refresher training includes an evaluation of its effectiveness. Score that evaluation on the new truck itself.

faq_plan.q: Does a forklift operator evaluation form work on a tablet on the warehouse floor?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The evaluator scores each maneuver on a tablet or phone while walking beside the truck, and both people sign on the same screen at the end. An app Emergent builds has no response cap, and every evaluation stays on file for as long as you keep the app.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a forklift operator evaluation form when hiring operators?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a short practical on your own truck after the interview. An interview evaluation form records what the candidate says about their experience. The practical shows whether they can move a load the way your site expects. Keep both with the applicant's file.
